headline: {arm:brisk-s.low.r1} is the only configuration inside both gates, but by just {criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.gap|abs|pts} points on pass rate: re-test it on fresh cases before shipping, and decide now which gate gives if it fails.
lede: It is the cheapest configuration that clears the pass-rate gate, at {cost_per_month.brisk-s.low.r1} a month. If a re-test puts it below {criteria.pass_rate.threshold}, no configuration clears both gates.
flag: The snapshot holds no interval on pass rate or latency, so the pick's clearance rests on point estimates, and it is the one configuration of {n_candidates|int} that landed inside both gates, which makes its estimate optimistic.

caveats.material_if: only if the pick's true pass rate is below the gate, which a clearance this thin with no interval leaves open; then no configuration passes both gates.
only if the pick landed inside the gate partly by luck, as the one configuration of the sweep that did; a re-run on fresh cases would show it.
only if production carries more multi-hop or ambiguous-entity queries than the eval set, since the pick is below the gate on both and the gate reads the overall rate.
only if production p95 under load runs more than {criteria.p95.brisk-s.low.r1.gap} above the eval harness's, which is the pick's whole headroom.

decision.text: Re-test {arm:brisk-s.low.r1} and ship it if it holds. It passes {pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1} of queries against a gate of {criteria.pass_rate.threshold}, its p95 latency is {measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.low.r1.p95} against a budget of {criteria.p95.threshold}, and nothing else passes both.

{arm:brisk-s.high.r1} passes more often but its p95 is {measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.high.r1.p95}. Every Atlas-M configuration misses the latency budget, the fastest at {measure.latency_ms.atlas-m.off.r0.p95}. No Nano-XS configuration reaches the pass-rate gate; the best is {measure.pass_rate.nano-xs.high.r1.mean}. Brisk-S without a retry stays below the pass-rate gate at every reasoning level.

The pass-rate clearance of {criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.gap|abs|pts} points is the weakest margin on the page, and it sits on the pick. The latency headroom, {criteria.p95.brisk-s.low.r1.gap}, is one harness measurement with no interval, not production latency under load. Multi-hop queries, at {task.multihop.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.mean}, are where the pick is weakest.
Re-test the pick on fresh cases, pass rate and p95 both. If it holds, ship it; if it falls below either gate, the owner's declared fallback decides.

claims.text: {arm:brisk-s.low.r1} is the only one of the {n_candidates|int} configurations inside both gates, and it clears the pass-rate gate by {criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.gap|abs|pts} points. A retry is what lifts it over: a retry raises pass rate in every model and reasoning setting, for a few cents per thousand.

evidence.caption: Every model, reasoning level and retry setting: pass rate, cost, p95 latency and whether it passes both gates. The cost label is the renderer's; Method gives the basis.
The Brisk-S configurations, which sit nearest the corner where both gates hold; the lattice above holds all of them.

claims.text: On Brisk-S the retry lengthens only the latency tail: without it the pick's p95 would be {measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.low.r0.p95}. The step from low to high reasoning is what crosses the budget.

evidence.caption: Brisk-S latency from p50 to p95 against the p95 budget; one eval-harness measurement per configuration, no interval.

claims.text: Only relaxing the latency budget reaches a configuration that clears the pass-rate gate by more than the pick; the cheapest it would admit, {arm:brisk-s.high.r1}, runs {cost_per_month.brisk-s.high.r1} a month.

evidence.caption: The pick and every configuration that clears the pass-rate gate: pass rate, cost per thousand calls as the snapshot measures it, and p95 latency.

claims.text: Multi-hop queries are the pick's weakest type, at {task.multihop.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.mean}; the one multi-hop failure the snapshot froze collapses the chain of lookups into a single search. Its ambiguous-entity failure is scored wrong for answering without asking which entity was meant, so that type's rate also rests on the gold answers requiring a clarifying question.

evidence.caption: Pass rate by query type for the pick and the same model with high reasoning; the gate reads the overall rate, so no line is drawn.
The snapshot froze one failure per query type for the pick, three in all; they illustrate and don't measure.

explore.binds: which configuration is the cheapest that passes both gates
explore.outcome: Above {pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1} nothing passes. The pick holds for any gate above {pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r0}. Lower the gate and the pick steps down: {arm:brisk-s.low.r0} at or below {pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r0}, {arm:nano-xs.high.r1} at or below {pass_rate.nano-xs.high.r1}, {arm:nano-xs.low.r1} at or below {pass_rate.nano-xs.low.r1}, {arm:nano-xs.off.r1} at or below {pass_rate.nano-xs.off.r1}, and {arm:nano-xs.off.r0} at or below {pass_rate.nano-xs.off.r0}.

explore.binds: whether the pick has a rival
explore.outcome: Below {measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.low.r1.p95} nothing passes. From {measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.high.r1.p95} up, {arm:brisk-s.high.r1} passes too and clears the pass-rate gate by {criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.high.r1.gap|abs|pts} points. The pick stays the call there only if the cheaper option wins; the campaign declared no rule ranking cost against clearance.

omitted.why: Describes planner behavior and no gate reads it. It bears on cost only if cost is per call, which Method addresses; the order of the configurations that clear the pass-rate gate is the same on either basis.
Listed in the campaign but hold no figures in this snapshot.
The budget is on p95; the median binds nothing. It is in the appendix tables.

omitted.why: Its point labels print internal ids once every configuration is drawn; the lattice shows all of them by name and the scatter keeps the Brisk-S row, which holds the corner.

next.text: The owner declares which gate gives if the re-test fails: the latency budget (then {arm:brisk-s.high.r1} passes, at {cost_per_month.brisk-s.high.r1} a month) or the pass-rate gate (then the step-down in Explore applies).
next.settles: The fallback, decided before the re-test result can bias it.

next.text: Re-run {arm:brisk-s.low.r1} on fresh cases, several times the current set, reporting intervals on pass rate and p95.
next.settles: Whether it really clears both gates, or the pass-rate clearance was the luck of being the one configuration inside.

next.text: Measure the pick's p95 under production-like load.
next.settles: Whether its latency headroom survives outside the eval harness.

next.text: Read a sample of the pick's multi-hop failures, then, if the collapsed-chain pattern holds, add a multi-hop planning directive and re-run multi-hop and ambiguous-entity queries.
next.settles: Whether the thin margin can widen without paying for more reasoning; today the pattern rests on one frozen failure.

next.text: Declare the production mix of query types, or weight the eval set to it.
next.settles: Whether the overall rate the gate reads matches the traffic the planner will see.

method.text: {scoreboard.brisk-s.low.r1.cases|int} queries per configuration, the same for all {n_candidates|int}; no repeats are recorded and no trials were lost.
Every model at every reasoning level, with and without a retry, fully crossed; no control or production configuration was included, so nothing is read as a change from current behavior.

The snapshot doesn't define what makes a query pass. The failures it records are a missing call, wrong arguments or the wrong tool against an expected plan; an ambiguous query answered without a clarifying question counts as a failure.
None. Every figure on the page is a point estimate, latency included; no correction applies because no contrast is tested.
Pass rate at least {criteria.pass_rate.threshold} overall and p95 latency at most {criteria.p95.threshold}, measured in the eval harness; neither is marked as set after the results.
None: pass is a recorded check, not a judged score.

The snapshot names its cost measure per thousand calls, the lattice prints it as per 1,000 replies, and the monthly figures multiply it by the monthly volume of {meta.volume_per_month|int} as if both counted queries. If cost is per tool call, each query costs more by its calls per task ({measure.calls_per_task.brisk-s.low.r1.mean} for the pick) and the monthly figures understate. The order of the configurations that clear the pass-rate gate is the same on either basis.
Synthetic example data, as the snapshot's provenance states.
